title: Flat point sections and normalized ordinary scalar extension
statement:
theorem pointFiniteReductionSectionAlgebra (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] :
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (M : pointFiniteReductionSheaves k l E n),
      SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1}
        (R := pointFiniteReductionRingSheaf k l E n) M →
      Module.Flat (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n))
        ((pointFiniteSections k (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n)).obj M)) ∧
    ∀ (n j : ℕ) (h : j ≤ n),
      ∃ e : pointFiniteSections k (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n) ⋙
          ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} (pointFiniteReductionRingMap l E n j h) ≅
        pointFiniteReductionSheafExtension k l E n j h ⋙
          pointFiniteSections k (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E j),
        ∀ (M : pointFiniteReductionSheaves k l E n)
          (b : ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E j))
          (x : (pointFiniteSections k (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n)).obj M),
          e.hom.app M (b ⊗ₜ[_, pointFiniteReductionRingMap l E n j h] x) =
            b • pointFiniteReductionSectionGenerator k l E n j h M x
Definitions and coefficient conventions: [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

source.place: Proof (1), the reductions of $P_{n+1}$ and $P_{\bar y,n+1}$, where the point fibre $\operatorname{Fib}_s=\Gamma(s,-)$ of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point and the stalk at a geometric point are applied to a sheaf-level reduction isomorphism without a statement of their compatibility with $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_{n+1}}A_n$; the integral analogue is lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction

proof.text: The constant presheaf sheafification unit at the final point is bijective, hence the coefficient-to-final-sections ring map is a ring equivalence.

For a finite linear relation in the sections of a flat module sheaf, use the local equational criterion. The covering sieve contains the identity, so the witnesses are global. Transport their coefficients through the constant-section ring equivalence. The ordinary module equational criterion proves flatness of the sections.

Transport the tensor product through the source and target constant-section ring equivalences. Final sections of the sheafified tensor presheaf equal its presheaf sections, and the prescribed ordinary object equation identifies them with the chosen extension. Naturality follows from the sheafification unit and the prescribed map equation. On b tensor x this is exactly b times the sheafification-unit section x. The proof also covers n=j, j=0, the zero module and infinite modules.
